title: How do we read a five digit number in words?
description: Meera sees a five digit number on a board at the village fair in Odisha. The video reads it in words and splits it into an expanded form.
teaching_notes: One idea: the comma stands for the word thousand. Watch for the child who skips the word thousand.

source: Write 45,867 in words and in expanded form.
video_script.why: The child can name numbers up to about fourteen thousand but has not read a large five digit number.
video_script.substitution: Read the part before the comma, say thousand, then read the last three digits; add the place values back for the expanded form.
video_script.anchor: a visitors board at a village fair in Odisha that Meera passes
video_script.wrong_answer: forty five, eight hundred sixty seven
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu reads the comma as a pause and skips the word thousand. The comma stands for the word thousand.
video_script.payoff_line: the comma stands for the word thousand

final_answer.value: Forty-five thousand eight hundred sixty-seven, and 45,867 = 40,000 + 5,000 + 800 + 60 + 7
final_answer.spoken: forty five thousand eight hundred sixty seven

maths_rules: the number is 45,867: TTh 4, Th 5, H 8, T 6, O 7
part before the comma: 45, said forty five, then the word thousand
last three digits: 867, said eight hundred sixty seven
name: forty five thousand eight hundred sixty seven
slip: skipping the word thousand reads 45,867 as forty five, eight hundred sixty seven
your turn: 62,304 = 60,000 + 2,000 + 300 + 0 + 4, the name is sixty two thousand three hundred four; never shown
video_script.design: One idea: say the part before the comma, then thousand, then the last three digits. Wrong idea: skipping the word thousand. The fair board stays as the anchor; the chart and the sum build on the stage.

narration: <bookmark mark='front'/>Read the part before the comma first. It is forty five.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>The comma stands for the word thousand, so we say it there.
<bookmark mark='back'/>Then read the last three digits, eight hundred sixty seven.
<bookmark mark='name'/>The full name is forty five thousand eight hundred sixty seven.

beats.on_screen: the digits split into place values on the board: 40,000 + 5,000 + 800 + 60 + 7 = 45,867

narration: <bookmark mark='def'/>Writing a number as the sum of its place values is called expanded form.
<bookmark mark='parts'/>Four in the TTh place is forty thousand, and five in the Th place is five thousand.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>Then come eight hundred, sixty and seven, to finish the sum.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Add them all and we get the number back.
